problems.title: Global and local extrema of a cosine quadratic
problems.question: Find the minimum and maximum points of f(x)=cos²x+cosx+1.
problems.idea: First use t=cosx; also check local maxima at t=-1.
steps: The global minimum is 3/4 when cosx=-1/2, at x=2πk±2π/3.
The global maximum is 3 when cosx=1, at x=2πk.
At x=(2k+1)π, cosx=-1 and f=1. Near these points cosx>-1 makes f<1, so these are additional local maxima.
problems.answer: Global minima: (2πk±2π/3,3/4); global maxima: (2πk,3). Other local maxima: ((2k+1)π,1), k∈ℤ.
problems.note: The word “maximum” may mean global or local. Both are listed so no valid local maximum is lost.

problems.title: Range of a cubic on a closed interval
problems.question: Find the range of y=x²(2x-3)-12(3x-2) on [-3,6].
problems.idea: Compare endpoints and every interior stationary point.
steps: The stationary points are x=-2,3, both in the interval.
A continuous function attains its extremes among these candidates, giving minimum -57 and maximum 132.

problems.title: A common tangent to two parabolas
problems.question: Find the common tangent to y=x²-2x+5 and y=x²+2x-11.
problems.idea: A tangent intersects each quadratic with discriminant zero.
formulas: For y=x²+bx+c, a tangent y=mx+d satisfies d=c-(b-m)²/4.
steps: The two conditions are d=5-(m+2)²/4 and d=-11-(m-2)²/4.
Equating them gives 16=[(m+2)²-(m-2)²]/4=2m, so m=8.
Then d=5-25=-20. The contact x-values are 5 and 3 respectively.

problems.title: An increasing interval with a decreasing logarithm base
problems.question: Find where $f(x)=\log_{1/3}(x^2+x-2)$ increases.
problems.idea: Include the logarithm’s domain in the derivative sign test.
steps: The argument (x+2)(x-1)>0 gives x<-2 or x>1.
On the domain the denominator is negative because ln(1/3)<0.
The derivative is positive when 2x+1<0, which intersects the domain in x<-2.

problems.title: Largest cylinder inside a cone
problems.question: A cone has radius R and height h. Find the greatest volume of an inscribed coaxial cylinder.
problems.idea: Similarity links the cylinder radius to its height.
steps: Let u=H/h with 0≤u≤1. The variable part is u(1-u)².
Its derivative is (1-u)(1-3u), so its maximum occurs at u=1/3; both endpoints give zero.
Thus H=h/3,r=2R/3 and V=π(2R/3)²(h/3).

problems.title: A cubic increasing everywhere
problems.question: Find all a for which $f(x)=(a^2-1)x^3/3+(a-1)x^2+2x+1$ is increasing on ℝ.
problems.idea: Its quadratic derivative must never be negative.
formulas: f′=(a²-1)x²+2(a-1)x+2; a quadratic with positive leading coefficient is nonnegative everywhere iff its discriminant is ≤0.
steps: For a²-1>0, the discriminant is 4(a-1)²-8(a²-1)=-4(a-1)(a+3).
Thus a<-1 or a>1, together with (a-1)(a+3)≥0, gives a≤-3 or a>1.
If a=1, f′=2 works. If a=-1, f′=-4x+2 fails. If |a|<1, the derivative eventually becomes negative.
At a=-3 the derivative vanishes only at one point; the function still strictly increases.

problems.title: An ellipse tangent to one axis
problems.question: An axis-aligned ellipse touches the y-axis at (0,5) and meets the x-axis at (5,0),(11,0). Find its equation.
problems.idea: The tangency point fixes the centre’s y-coordinate; the two crossings are symmetric.
steps: The centre is (8,5), since the x-intercepts have midpoint x=8 and the y-axis tangency is at centre height 5.
The horizontal semiaxis is A=8. At (5,0), 9/64+25/B²=1, so B²=320/11.
Insert these values into the ellipse equation.

problems.title: There are two parallel tangents
problems.question: Find the tangents to x²+y²+5x=0 perpendicular to 4x-3y+7=0.
problems.idea: A circle has two supporting tangents in a fixed direction.
steps: The given line has slope 4/3, so each desired tangent has slope -3/4: 3x+4y+c=0.
Tangency gives |c-15/2|/5=5/2.
Thus c=20 or c=-5.
problems.note: Both tangents satisfy the requirement; one line alone would be incomplete.

problems.title: Hyperbola from its asymptotes and one point
problems.question: Find the hyperbola with asymptotes $y=\pm3x/5$ passing through $(10,-3\sqrt3)$.
problems.idea: The asymptotes fix the centre and semiaxis ratio.
steps: Set B²=9A²/25. Substitution of the point gives 100/A²-27/(9A²/25)=1.
Thus 25/A²=1, so A²=25,B²=9.

problems.title: A parabola parameter from a hyperbola distance
problems.question: A parabola has vertex (0,0), opens in the negative x direction, and has |p| equal to the distance from a focus of 4x²-9y²-36=0 to an asymptote. Find its equation.
problems.idea: Find the distance first and state the parabola convention.
formulas: Hyperbola x²/a²-y²/b²=1 has c²=a²+b² and asymptotes y=±bx/a; parabola convention y²=2px.
steps: The hyperbola is x²/9-y²/4=1, with focus (√13,0) and asymptote 2x-3y=0.
The distance is 2√13/√13=2. Thus |p|=2 and the left-opening direction gives p=-2.
Using y²=2px, the equation is y²=-4x.
problems.note: Some books define p by y²=4px instead. With that different parameter convention the same stated |p|=2 would give y²=-8x. The convention must be specified.
